protocol.label_en: Credential-agile two-message mutually authenticated key exchange
protocol.label_zh: 凭据敏捷的两消息双向认证密钥交换

overview_classification.summary_label_zh: 覆盖 KEM/签名四种有序凭据组合的两消息双向认证 AKE 套件

authentication.mechanism: K-credential holders authenticate by recovery of secrets encapsulated to long-term KEM keys; S-credential holders authenticate signed transcript components. All four K2S/S2K/K2K/S2S frameworks provide mutual authentication.

roles.key_details: Long-term credential type is KEM in K2S/K2K and signature in S2K/S2S; always creates an ephemeral wKEM/second-2KEM key pair.
Long-term credential type is signature in K2S/S2S and KEM in S2K/K2K; encapsulates to the initiator ephemeral key and may sign the response.

pre_distributed_material: Authenticated long-term public credential for each peer (KEM or signature according to framework profile)

forward_secrecy.conditions: The IND-(St)AA model captures weak forward secrecy for completed honest sessions, subject to each framework's freshness restrictions on long-term-key and session-state reveals.

protocol_characteristics.key_confirmation: Implicit mutual authentication/key agreement within two messages; no third explicit confirmation message is specified.
protocol_characteristics.transcript_binding: H derives the session key from both identities/public credentials, the complete public transcript, and all KEM-derived secrets used by the selected framework.
protocol_characteristics.identity_binding: pki and pkj are inputs to H in every framework; signature verification or long-term KEM decapsulation binds the appropriate credential holder to the transcript.

technical_classification.construction_paradigm: Four-framework credential-type matrix: K2S and S2K combine an ephemeral IND-CPA wKEM, a long-term IND-CCA KEM and one signature; K2K combines a double-key KEM with a responder KEM contribution; S2S combines an ephemeral wKEM with two signatures.

protocol_flow.semantics: Initiator retains fsk and fpk as session state.

components.name: ec
components.semantics: wKEM ciphertext to fpk, yielding ek.

components.name: ci
components.semantics: IND-CCA KEM ciphertext to initiator long-term KEM public key, yielding ki.

components.name: sigma
components.semantics: Responder signature over fpk || ec || ci.

components.name: fpk
components.semantics: Ephemeral wKEM public key derived from G(ski,er).

components.name: cj
components.semantics: KEM ciphertext to responder long-term KEM key, yielding kj.

protocol_flow.semantics: Initiator stores er, cj and kj.

components.name: ec
components.semantics: wKEM ciphertext to fpk, yielding ek.

protocol_flow.semantics: After signature verification and decapsulation, both derive H(pki,pkj,fpk,ec,cj,kj,ek).

components.name: fpk
components.semantics: Fresh second public key for 2KEM, derived from G(r,ski).

components.name: cj
components.semantics: KEM ciphertext to responder long-term key, yielding kj.

protocol_flow.semantics: Initiator stores r, kj and cj.

components.name: ci
components.semantics: Double-key ciphertext encapsulated jointly to initiator long-term pki and ephemeral fpk, yielding ki.

components.name: fpk
components.semantics: Ephemeral wKEM public key derived from G(ski,er).

components.name: ec
components.semantics: wKEM ciphertext to fpk, yielding ek.

protocol_flow.semantics: After reciprocal signature verification, both derive H(pki,pkj,fpk,ec,ek).

static_contributions: Long-term KEM contribution ki or kj in K2S/S2K/K2K.
Long-term signing keys authenticate signed transcript components in K2S/S2K/S2S but are not direct secret entropy inputs to H.
In S2K/S2S/K2K, G mixes the initiator long-term secret key with fresh randomness when regenerating ephemeral key material.
ephemeral_contributions: ek from the ephemeral wKEM in K2S/S2K/S2S.
ki from joint long-term/ephemeral 2KEM encapsulation in K2K.
Fresh er or r determines the initiator ephemeral/second key pair in S2K/K2K/S2S.
key_schedule.transcript_hash: No separate T variable; H directly absorbs pki, pkj, fpk, all ciphertexts, and all KEM-derived secrets for the selected framework.
key_schedule.session_key_derivation: K2S/S2K: K=H(pki,pkj,fpk,ec,c_long,k_long,ek); K2K: K=H(pki,pkj,fpk,ci,cj,ki,kj); S2S: K=H(pki,pkj,fpk,ec,ek).
key_schedule.domain_separation: No explicit textual domain-separation labels were located; framework-specific ordered inputs and credential/public-key values separate contexts.
key_schedule.ephemeral_secret_erasure: Implementations include secure_bzero support; the specification's exposure analysis treats stored session state explicitly, but a complete normative erasure schedule was not located.

correctness.relationship: Except for the two compact K2K constructions, the submission states that AKE failure is inherited from the corresponding KEM instantiation. Compact K2K combines CCA-KEM and CPA-PKE failure events and gives explicit aggregate bounds.
correctness.basis: Specification p.16 and practical-security Tables 2-4, pp.26-27.

security_claims.claim: All four credential-order frameworks provide mutual authentication using KEM-secret recovery, signatures, or both.
K2S and S2S are analyzed under IND-AA; S2K and K2K use the applicable IND-StAA session-state-reveal model.
The IND-(St)AA framework captures weak forward secrecy for completed honest sessions.
Session-key pseudorandomness reduces to wKEM IND-CPA, KEM IND-CCA or 2KEM [IND-CCA,IND-CPA], signature EUF-CMA, and QROM assumptions as applicable.

claimed_advantages.claim: A complete ordered matrix covers both KEM/signature migration directions and both homogeneous credential deployments.
Every submitted instance completes mutual authentication and key establishment in two messages (one round trip).
Frameworks use black-box KEM, signature and double-key-KEM interfaces and can be extended with compatible primitive families.
Reference and AVX2 implementations cover all 25 instances; K2K gives the lowest measured computational profile and ZEN-based instances generally the smallest complete exchanges.
Generic and structure-aware compact double-key KEM routes provide alternative bandwidth profiles, including compact PolarLAC K2K at 512-bit security.

limitations_and_constraints.description: Each endpoint must possess and authenticate the peer's long-term public credential of the profile-selected type.
Security analyses model H and G as quantum-accessible random oracles.
KEM-based components have nonzero decryption-failure probabilities; compact double-key ciphertext combination increases DFR and is used only where margin permits.
S2K, K2K and S2S derive ephemeral key material from a long-term secret plus stored session randomness to meet their reveal model; exposure conditions remain constrained by IND-(St)AA freshness.
Concrete instances depend on separately submitted PolarLAC, ZEN and BiT primitives and inherit the minimum security strength of their components.
Benchmarks average 10,000 executions on one Intel Core i7-1360P system under Ubuntu 24.04.1/WSL2; only portable C and x86-64 AVX2 are reported.
For heterogeneous profiles, the standard single long-term-key size field cannot represent both credential types; per-role values are stored in core_parameters and the scalar field is null.
